diagnosis: Granular cell tumour of the subcutaneous tissue in the chest wall
legend: Dissociated cells with rounded nuclei, showing some crush artefact, and abundant dense cytoplasm. The features are atypical, and the differential diagnosis is of granular cell tumour and an apocrine neoplasm (Giemsa).

diagnosis: Granular cell tumour of the subcutaneous tissue in the chest wall
legend: Corresponding section of a benign granular cell tumour (H&E).

A tissue fragment of myxoid stroma with embedded spindle nuclei showing mild hyperchromatism and branching vasculature. There is a broad differential diagnosis, and the features are categorized as “Atypical” (Giemsa).

Dissociated spindle nuclei showing some size variation and hyperchromatism, and a variable amount of cytoplasm. The features raise a broad differential diagnosis and are categorized as “Atypical”, suggestive of a spindle cell neoplasm (Giemsa).
A circumscribed myxoid lesion arising in the breast, with no cytopathological features of malignancy, most consistent with a myxoid myofibroblastoma (tissue section, H&E).
